hotpotqa.summary: 2018 multi-hop Wikipedia questions with 10 given paragraphs; Yugos grades the labelled distractor validation set by joint answer+evidence F1. As the live set, only the questions outside the live 70 (plus the 90k train split) can train the router. Anchor scores are zero-shot answer scores (StreamBench, 1,500 dev questions, metric presumably EM), which is easier than Yugos's joint F1; the Yugos IRT fit puts ~91% of the live questions at L4-5 because of that strict grading.

chat.why: Real WildChat requests with new verifiable output constraints (median ~73 tokens): single prompt, but the answer is free text checked by constraint functions, not a short exact answer.

ifbench.licence: ODC-BY-1.0 (data, per GitHub README; code Apache-2.0)
ifbench.summary: 300 prompts from held-out WildChat with 58 new out-of-distribution constraints (format, word, count, ratio...), graded by verification functions (prompt-level loose in the paper). Fresh (2025) and checkable, but instruction following is not in any public Yugos chat set, so it can only be a guess at the private chat mix. Anchor scores are Artificial Analysis runs as stored in the step1-benchmark DB; the AA page itself only showed the top 3.

kor_bench.summary: 1,250 'knowledge-orthogonal' reasoning questions (5 categories x 25 rules x 10), e.g. 'Compute 4※7' after a rule defines ※, or decrypt with a given cipher; exact-match answers. A good stand-in for bbeh-style public chat reasoning; GPT-4o scores 58%, so mostly L2-L3. No per-model per-question outcomes found.
